Key Finding: Housing insecurity is associated with lower student success and poorer mental well-being, strengthening the case for timely housing information.
APA Reference: Kornbluh, M., Wilking, J., Roll, S., & Donatello, R. (2024). Exploring housing insecurity in relation to student success. Journal of American College Health, 72(3), 680–684. https://doi.org/10.1080/07448481.2022.2068016

Key Finding: In an Australian pilot study, housing insecurity or homelessness coincided with significantly lower university engagement and well-being among tertiary students.
APA Reference: Purcell, T., & Davidson, D. (2026). Young university students experiences of homelessness and housing insecurity. Social Sciences, 15(11), 736. https://doi.org/10.3390/socsci15110736

Key Finding: Philippine lodging houses and dormitories housed 78,812 institutional residents in 2024, showing that this form of accommodation is a substantial housing context.
APA Reference: Philippine Statistics Authority. (2026). Institutional population of the Philippines based on the 2024 Census. https://psa.gov.ph/statistics/population-and-housing?page=15

Key Finding: Collaborative web maps commonly depend on non-expert geographic contributions, making formal data-management and quality practices important to system design.
APA Reference: Pedregal, B., Orozco, G., Osorio, J., & Díaz-Cuevas, P. (2024). Characterizing collaborative mapping projects. Transactions in GIS, 28, 1908–1927. https://doi.org/10.1111/tgis.13210

Key Finding: Volunteer geographic information can vary in accuracy and trustworthiness, while multiple observers can support consensus-based validation.
APA Reference: Foody, G. M., See, L., Fritz, S., Van der Velde, M., Perger, C., Schill, C., & Boyd, D. S. (2013). Assessing the accuracy of volunteered geographic information. Transactions in GIS, 17(6), 847–860. https://doi.org/10.1111/tgis.12033

Key Finding: Crowdsourced geographic information can be assessed through multiple quality methods even when authoritative reference data are unavailable.
APA Reference: Degrossi, L. C., Albuquerque, J. P., Rocha, R. S., & Zipf, A. (2018). A taxonomy of quality assessment methods for volunteered and crowdsourced geographic information. Transactions in GIS, 22(2), 542–560. https://doi.org/10.1111/tgis.12329

Key Finding: Global housing shortages and rising price-to-income ratios are deepening affordability pressures, especially for vulnerable households.
APA Reference: United Nations Human Settlements Programme. (2026). World cities report 2026. https://unhabitat.org/sites/default/files/2026/05/wcr_2026.pdf

Key Finding: Philippine total housing expenditure increased from about PHP 1.20 trillion in 2018 to PHP 1.63 trillion in 2023.
APA Reference: Philippine Statistics Authority. (2026). Total housing expenditure by income decile: 2018, 2021, and 2023. https://openstat.psa.gov.ph

Key Finding: Philippine rental regulation for units at or below PHP 10,000 includes boarding houses, dormitories, rooms, and student bed spaces.
APA Reference: Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development. (2024). National Human Settlements Board Resolution No. 2024-01. https://dhsud.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/Laws_Issuances/07_NHSB/NHSB%20Resolution%202024-01%20%28Rent%20Control%202025-2026%29.pdf

Key Finding: Climate-driven heavy precipitation can overwhelm urban roads, buildings, transportation systems, and storm-water drainage.
APA Reference: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change. (2021). Climate information relevant for the cities, buildings, and transport sectors. https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg1/downloads/factsheets/IPCC_AR6_WGI_Sectoral_Fact_Sheet_Cities_Buildings_Transport.pdf

Key Finding: Buildings and construction account for about 37% of global energy- and process-related carbon dioxide emissions and over 34% of energy demand.
APA Reference: United Nations Environment Programme. (n.d.). Buildings. https://www.unep.org/en/what-we-do/energy/buildings

Key Finding: Climate action in buildings can reduce energy bills, improve living conditions, and strengthen resilience while lowering emissions.
APA Reference: United Nations Environment Programme. (2026). Climate action key to affordable housing, but buildings decarbonisation stalls. https://www.unep.org/en/news-and-stories/press-release/climate-action-key-affordable-housing-buildings-decarbonisation

Key Finding: The Philippine Urban Development and Housing Act establishes a comprehensive and continuing housing program involving government and private-sector cooperation.
APA Reference: Republic of the Philippines. (1992). Republic Act No. 7279: Urban Development and Housing Act of 1992. https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1992/ra_7279_1992.html

Key Finding: CHED and Pag-IBIG Fund’s Project BALAY links student housing with education and social development to support higher-education completion.
APA Reference: Commission on Higher Education. (n.d.). CHED, Pag-IBIG Fund partner to expand student housing under Project BALAY. https://legacy.ched.gov.ph/ched-pag-ibig-fund-partner-to-expand-student-housing-under-project-balay/

Key Finding: The National Human Settlements Board directs DHSUD to consider rental assistance and public rental housing with local governments during the rent-control transition.
APA Reference: Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development. (2024). National Human Settlements Board Resolution No. 2024-01. https://dhsud.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/Laws_Issuances/07_NHSB/NHSB%20Resolution%202024-01%20%28Rent%20Control%202025-2026%29.pdf

Key Finding: The Philippine Data Privacy Act protects personal information in government and private information systems while supporting lawful information flows.
APA Reference: Republic of the Philippines. (2012). Republic Act No. 10173: Data Privacy Act of 2012. https://officialgazette.gov.ph/2012/08/15/republic-act-no-10173/

Key Finding: The Philippine privacy rules require transparency, legitimate purpose, proportionality, data quality, limited retention, and secure disposal of personal data.
APA Reference: National Privacy Commission. (2016). Implementing rules and regulations of the Data Privacy Act of 2012. https://privacy.gov.ph/implementing-rules-regulations-data-privacy-act-2012/

Key Finding: The OECD Privacy Guidelines define collection limitation, purpose specification, use limitation, security safeguards, openness, participation, and accountability as data-protection principles.
APA Reference: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development. (2013). The OECD privacy guidelines. https://legalinstruments.oecd.org/en/instruments/OECD-LEGAL-0188

Key Finding: The Belmont Report identifies respect for persons, beneficence, and justice as core principles, requiring consent, minimized harm, and fair treatment.
APA Reference: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. (1979). The Belmont report. https://www.hhs.gov/ohrp/regulations-and-policy/belmont-report/read-the-belmont-report/index.html

Key Finding: Location-based services can reduce users’ control over accurate location data, so ethical analysis must address context, purpose limitation, and privacy.
APA Reference: Herrmann, M., Hildebrandt, M., Tielemans, L., & Diaz, C. (2016). Privacy in location-based services: An interdisciplinary approach. SCRIPTed, 13(2). https://doi.org/10.2966/scrip.130216.144

Key Finding: Geodata may identify people or sensitive places even after aggregation, requiring context-sensitive anonymization and responsible dissemination.
APA Reference: Solymosi, R., Buil-Gil, D., Ceccato, V., Kim, E., & Jansson, U. (2023). Privacy challenges in geodata and open data. Area, 55(4), 456–464. https://doi.org/10.1111/area.12888
